newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland to link to ERM at 3.04/mark - supervisor.
newsitem.headline: Finland to link to ERM at 3.04/mark - supervisor.

text.p: Finland will link its currency, the markka, to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) at a central parity rate of 3.04 to the mark, central bank supervisor Kimmo Sasi told Reuters on Saturday.
"It is 3.04 markka per German mark," he said.
"The ECU central rate of the Finnish markka has been agreed to be FIM 5.80661," the government said in a statement which said Finland had joined Europe's currency stability mechanism.

"Through participation in the exchange rate mechanism, the Finnish government wants to guarantee that Finland will fulfil all the convergence criteria related to the third stage of economic and monetary union," the statement.
The markka was trading at 2.986 to the German mark at the close of business on Friday. @

In Brussels, the monetary committee said in a statement the markka would be allowed to fluctuate by up to 15 percent against other currencies in the grid, the normal margins since the ERM bands were widened in August 1993 after severe pressure on the system.

The markka has been floating freely since September 8, 1992. It was briefly linked unilaterally to the European Currency Unit (Ecu) between June and November 1991, when it was devalued by around 12 percent and then re-linked to the Ecu.
But strong foreign exchange market speculation forced it further down in value, and it has since been left to float freely.
